Simulate U-BOIN Trials

Source: R/uboin_simulate.R
uboin_simulate.Rd

Simulate trials of the utility-based BOIN (U-BOIN) phase I/II design of Zhou, Lee and Yuan (2019), which looks for the optimal biological dose (OBD) from a binary toxicity and a binary efficacy outcome observed before the next cohort is treated. This is the simulation engine behind sim_uboin, exposed for users who want the raw trial data.

Usage

uboin_simulate(
  tox_upper,
  resp_lower,
  p_true = NULL,
  p_resp = NULL,
  n_cohort,
  cohort_size,
  n_trials = 10000,
  target = NULL,
  resp_assoc = 0,
  p_outcome = NULL,
  utility = c(0, 30, 50, 100),
  n_stage1 = 12,
  n_stop = NULL,
  start_dose = 1,
  p_saf = NULL,
  p_tox = NULL,
  cutoff_eli = 0.95,
  cutoff_eli_resp = 0.9,
  prior_tox = c(1, 1),
  prior_resp = c(1, 1),
  seed = 123
)

Arguments

tox_upper

Numeric scalar. Highest acceptable DLT probability, for example 0.30.

resp_lower

Numeric scalar. Lowest acceptable response probability, for example 0.20.

p_true

Numeric vector or NULL. True DLT probability of each dose.

p_resp

Numeric vector or NULL. True response probability of each dose.

n_cohort

Integer scalar. Number of cohorts in a trial; the maximum sample size is n_cohort * cohort_size.

cohort_size

Integer scalar. Number of patients per cohort.

n_trials

Integer scalar. Number of trials to simulate. Defaults to 10000.

target

Numeric scalar or NULL. Target DLT probability of the BOIN design in stage I. Defaults to NULL, which uses tox_upper - 0.05.

resp_assoc

Numeric scalar. Association parameter of the Gumbel model that joins the DLT and the response of a patient; 0 makes them independent. Defaults to 0.

p_outcome

Numeric matrix or NULL. Probabilities of the four outcomes of a patient at each dose, one row per dose, in the columns (no response, DLT), (no response, no DLT), (response, DLT) and (response, no DLT). When given, p_true, p_resp and resp_assoc must be NULL or are not used. Defaults to NULL.

utility

Numeric vector of length four. Utility of the four outcomes, in the order of p_outcome. Defaults to c(0, 30, 50, 100), example 1 of the article.

n_stage1

Integer scalar. Stage II starts once a dose has this many patients (s1 of the article). Defaults to 12.

n_stop

Integer scalar or NULL. The trial ends once a dose has this many patients (s2 of the article). Defaults to NULL, the maximum sample size.

start_dose

Integer scalar. Dose level of the first cohort. Defaults to 1.

p_saf

Numeric scalar. Highest DLT probability deemed subtherapeutic, for the boundaries of stage I. Defaults to 0.6 * target.

p_tox

Numeric scalar. Lowest DLT probability deemed overly toxic, for the boundaries of stage I. Defaults to 1.4 * target.

cutoff_eli

Numeric scalar. A dose is toxic when the posterior probability that its DLT probability exceeds tox_upper is above this value. Defaults to 0.95.

cutoff_eli_resp

Numeric scalar. A dose is futile when the posterior probability that its response probability is below resp_lower is above this value. Defaults to 0.90.

prior_tox

Numeric vector of length two. Beta prior of the DLT probability in the toxicity rule. Defaults to c(1, 1).

prior_resp

Numeric vector of length two. Beta prior of the response probability in the futility rule. Defaults to c(1, 1).

seed

Integer scalar or NULL. Random seed. The state of the calling session is restored on exit. Defaults to 123.

Value

An object of class uboin_trials, which is a list with components

n_outcome

Integer array with dimensions trial by dose by outcome: number of patients with each outcome.

n_pts, n_tox, n_resp

Integer matrices with one row per trial and one column per dose: patients treated, DLTs and responses.

eliminated

Logical matrix: doses eliminated in stage I.

cohorts_used

Integer vector: cohorts treated in each trial.

stage2

Logical vector: whether each trial reached stage II.

stop_reason

Character vector: why each trial ended.

boundary

List of the boundaries of stage I.

design

"U-BOIN".

settings

List of the design parameters.

Details

Stage I is the BOIN design with the target target. After each cohort, a dose that is toxic and has at least three patients is eliminated together with every higher dose, and the trial stops when the lowest dose is eliminated; the next cohort escalates (unless the next dose is eliminated), stays or de-escalates by the boundaries. Once a dose has n_stage1 patients, stage II starts with the next cohort:

  • (B1) If the DLT rate observed at the highest dose tried is at most the escalation boundary, that dose is not the highest dose and the dose above it is not eliminated, the next cohort is treated at the dose above it.

  • (B2) Otherwise the next cohort is treated at the admissible dose with the largest posterior mean utility, the lowest among ties. A dose is admissible when it has been tried, is not eliminated, and is neither toxic nor futile. The trial stops, without an OBD, when no dose is admissible.

The trial ends at the maximum sample size or when a dose has n_stop patients. The posterior mean utility of a dose is sum(utility * (1/4 + n_k)) / (1 + n), the utilities weighted by the posterior means of the outcome probabilities under the Dirichlet(1/4, 1/4, 1/4, 1/4) prior of the article. Utilities are compared after rounding to ten decimals.

The article does not give the priors of the toxicity and futility rules. With Beta(1, 1) priors the simulations of the article are reproduced (inst/reproduce/reproduce_Zhou2019.R); the decision tables of its supporting information are reproduced with prior_resp = c(0.05, 0.05). The article does not say either whether the admissible doses of rule B2 include doses not yet tried; they do not here, which the simulations of the article support. The stage I elimination uses the toxicity rule, as the article describes. A dose that becomes toxic in stage II does not exclude the doses above it.

One uniform random variate is drawn per patient, in enrollment order, and the outcome is the first whose cumulative probability exceeds it.

Only the pick-the-winner allocation of the article is provided; the adaptive and equal randomization and the version for efficacy observed late (Section 2.5 of the article) are not.

Values of stop_reason are "max_sample_size", "n_stop", "lowest_dose_eliminated" and "no_admissible_dose".

References

Zhou, Y., Lee, J. J. and Yuan, Y. (2019). A utility-based Bayesian optimal interval (U-BOIN) phase I/II design to identify the optimal biological dose for targeted and immune therapies. Statistics in Medicine, 38(28), S5299-S5316. doi:10.1002/sim.8361

See also

sim_uboin, uboin_select_obd, uboin_utility_table

Examples

trials <- uboin_simulate(
  tox_upper = 0.30,
  resp_lower = 0.20,
  p_true = c(0.02, 0.15, 0.30, 0.45, 0.60),
  p_resp = c(0.20, 0.65, 0.65, 0.65, 0.65),
  n_cohort = 18,
  cohort_size = 3,
  resp_assoc = 0.2,
  n_trials = 200,
  seed = 123
)
trials
#> Simulated U-BOIN trials
#>   trials               : 200
#>   doses                : 5
#>   DLT upper limit      : 0.3
#>   response lower limit : 0.2
#>   cohorts              : 18 of size 3
#>   max sample size      : 54
#> 
#> Averages per trial:
#>                     DL1   DL2   DL3  DL4  DL5
#> Patients treated   6.00 31.22 12.70 3.57 0.51
#> DLTs observed      0.14  4.74  3.92 1.59 0.30
#> Responses observed 1.18 20.48  8.18 2.35 0.30
#> 
#> Trials reaching stage II: 100%
#> Reason for ending (%):
#> 
#>        max_sample_size                 n_stop lowest_dose_eliminated 
#>                    100                      0                      0 
#>     no_admissible_dose 
#>                      0
